newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-Metzler close to an acquisition.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Metzler close to an acquisition.

text.p: Metzler Group Inc, whose shares fell sharply last week, expects soon to announce at least one acquisition that could help ease concerns on Wall Street about its growth program, the company's chairman said.
"I am still planning on being able to make some announcements (regarding acquisitions) before the end of this month," Robert Maher, Metzler's chairman, told Reuters Monday.
"With our acquisition strategy that we're beginning to deploy, I believe we'll be able to maintain our position and grow our market share," he said in a telephone interview.
Metzler shares tumbled by as much as 5-7/8 Friday before closing off 3-1/4 at 24. At the time, the Deerfield, Ill.-based company said it knew of no reason for the price drop.
Metzler, which provides consulting services to utilities and energy-related companies, closed up 1/4 Monday at 24-1/4.
Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette Securities Corp said Monday the plunge from a 52-week high of 36-3/4 created a buying opportunity. It upgraded Metzler to buy from market performer.
DLJ said the selloff was not tied to a change in Metzler's business fundamentals but was the result of several factors, including concern about a lack of acquisition activity.

Maher expressed surprise that analysts would be concerned about the timetable for Metzler's acquisition strategy, since conversations with potential targets began about 30 days after the company's initial public offering was completed October 4.

"Those conversations have been moving along basically at the pace I anticipated," said Maher, who is also Metzler's president and chief executive officer. "We tried to communicate to the analysts that whenever you're dealing with management consultants there are multiple issues that have to be resolved in order to complete an acquisition."
Maher added it takes four to six months to progress from negotiations to a definitive agreement.

With regard to increased competition to lure management consultants, Maher said Metzler is on pace to achieve its goal of having 80 consulting professionals by the end of 1997. Metzler currently has a professional staff of 59, Maher said.

Maher also dismissed general concerns raised by DLJ on competition in the marketplace, particularly from Hagler Bailly Inc, a consulting firm in Virginia that filed an initial public offering of 3.15 million shares February 21.
"They're really a totally different type of firm in what they do," he said. "They pretty much operate in completely different circles (than we do)."
Maher also said he was comfortable with analysts' estimates of earnings of about $0.78 a share for 1997, compared to $0.40 in 1996.

"When we look at the competition, while a possibility would exist for these firms to continue to grow down the line, we're hoping to have about two-to-one size advantage over our nearest competitor," Maher said.
